question_text: Can your suppliers give you verified emissions data for each shipment, and from which date?
What would it cost you to obtain verified data, set against the extra certificate cost that default values create?
Can you give us your actual import volumes by product for the last full year, so we can replace our sector estimate?
Which of the figures we estimated are wrong enough to matter, and what are the right ones?
Which of your customer contracts let you raise prices when input costs rise, and how much notice do they need?
If you cannot pass this cost on, which budget line absorbs it next year?
Do you expect your imports of these goods to stay below the mass threshold next year, and what would push them over it?
Who inside your business tracks that volume, and would you tell us in the same year the threshold was crossed?
How is this year's loss being funded, and does that funding leave room for a new certificate cost?
When do you expect to return to positive EBITDA, and what does that plan assume about carbon costs?
Have you applied for authorised CBAM declarant status, and what is the application reference and the expected decision date?
If the authorisation is not in place before your next shipment arrives, who will act as the declarant for those goods?
Which countries did these goods come from in the last full year, by volume?
Can your customs agent give us the declared origin for each shipment?
What is in your transition plan that we cannot see in the figures we hold, and would explain why our own rating is lower than this screening?
Which mitigating actions are funded and in the current budget, and when do they complete?
How much of this volume could move to a supplier inside the EU or in an exempt country, and how long would that switch take?
What happens to your delivery schedule and your price if that one origin becomes unavailable?
